text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Nordic countries announced their intention to make 51 million Danish crowns available to the Baltic states to implement several projects.
- The Committee for Education and Culture wants the practice of granting citizenship for special merits to be revised so that only the president be entitled to recommend the candidates.
- Today, after almost a 5-month interval, delegations of Latvia and Lithuania will resume talks on the two countries maritime border.
- Latvia's Privatbanka announced the start of its own liquidation from March 10. On January 21, the bank's licence was cancelled by the Bank of Latvia.
- Latvia's electricity company, Latvenergo, announced a decision to have electricity tariffs increased by an average 9.6 percent from May 1.

- Police in Liepaja are looking for a Swedish professor, Jan Ake Dallenbrant, who disappeared early in the morning of March 9. Dallenbrant arrived in Liepaja to monitor the course of municipal elections in the city.
- Parliament's Committee for Human Rights has rejected the proposal of deputy Vladlen Dosortsev to allow non-citizens to be practicing lawyers.
- Cabinet members held a closed meeting at the ministry of interior to discuss plans to build up the country's eastern border.

- On March 11, Rigas Komercbanka signed a seven million dollar loan agreement with Dresdner Bank and Landesbank Schleswig-Holstein. This is the first case when a Latvian bank has been given a loan by foreign commercial banks.
